newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria sees bigger 97 result despite CA cost.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria sees bigger 97 result despite CA cost.

text.p: Bank Austria said on Sunday it expected to increase its earnings potential in 1997 despite estimates of a "substantial" charge against earnings stemming from the integration of Creditanstalt.
Asked whether market leader Bank Austria expected to take any charges against earnings due to the takeover of number two bank Creditanstalt, chief executive Gerhard Randa told Reuters:
"The charges against earnings will be substantial -- and still our earnings will be better in 1997."
Earlier, Randa said preliminary parent operating profit for 1996 rose five percent to 5.1 billion schillings and that net profit would be "a trace below last year's."
In 1995, Bank Austria turned in a net profit of 2.2 billion schillings.

Finance Minister Viktor Klima, in the early hours of Sunday, said the government would sell its control in Creditanstalt to arch-rival Bank Austria for 17.161 billion schillings, or 861 schillings per voting share. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 253
